### The Test of Personal Hardship
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/test-personal-hardship
Passage: Nehemiah 5:2
Points:
- Severe economic hardship and famine caused deep exhaustion and internal friction among the builders.
- Selfishness often masquerades as lack of resources when people cling to their comfortable lifestyles.
- Nehemiah strongly rebuked leaders who exploited vulnerable brethren with exorbitant interest rates.
- Genuine reformation requires obedience to God's Word in economic matters as well as religious ones.
- Giving faithfully tests obedience and proves that believers cherish God above financial security.

### Doctrine Matters for Deeds of Mercy
Author: Jonathan Parnell
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/doctrine-matters-for-deeds-of-mercy
Passage: Nehemiah 5:9
Points:
- The rebuilding effort was severely fractured when wealthy nobles exploited the poor with usury and enslavement.
- Nehemiah diagnosed the core issue as an absence of the fear of God among the leaders.
- How believers treat other people is directly determined by what they truly believe about God.
- Human failure in the restoration points to our need for a newly transformed heart.
- Christ became poor on our behalf so that His people could overflow with generous mercy.

### Devotional: Nehemiah 5
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/genesis-16-matthew-15-nehemiah-5-acts-15/
Passage: Nehemiah 5:8
Points:
- Taking financial advantage of other people's disasters violates compassion and God's law.
- The wealthy were silenced and convicted when confronted with the hypocrisy of enslaving their own brothers.
- Nehemiah's rebuke produced genuine repentance, full restitution, and the cancellation of unfair interest.
- Nehemiah's leadership carried authority because he personally refused to exploit his office for wealth.
- Rebuilding covenant community and practical compassion is far more vital than merely erecting physical walls.

### Power Point - December 7, 2005
Author: Jack Graham
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/powerpoint/power-point-december-7-2005-1367169.html
Passage: Nehemiah 5:1-11
Points:
- How a person handles material wealth is a primary measurement of spiritual character.
- Uncontrolled indebtedness and greedy lending create spiritual bondage and divide communities.
- Easy credit frequently tempts people to fund their personal desires rather than their actual needs.
- Nehemiah demanded immediate restitution of mortgaged lands and an end to usury.
- Mastering money requires honoring God first, giving generously, and trusting Him to provide.
